resources.string: Open Eh-ligible to start your countdown
Not affiliated with IRCC or the Government of Canada. Estimates only: always confirm with IRCC’s official tools before applying.
Eh-ligible counts the days until you can apply, using the official rule: 1,095 days in Canada in the 5 years before you apply. It notices your trips by itself, right on your phone.
When did you become a permanent resident?
The date on your Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR): the day you landed or were approved in Canada.
Before that, were you in Canada with status?
Each day as a visitor, student, worker or protected person in the 5-year window counts as half a day, up to 365 days.
No, I landed as a PR
For protected persons, use the date your claim was approved.

Add periods without status, or spent waiting for a refugee claim decision. They don’t count. Maintained status (waiting on an extension) does count. If you’re unsure about a period, IRCC says to leave it out.
List your trips since %1$s, day trips included. From today on, Eh-ligible notices new trips by itself.

Eh-ligible uses your approximate location to check which country you’re in when you open the app or tap the widget, so trips are counted automatically. The check happens on your phone: your location is never stored or sent anywhere.
Location checks are on. Thank you!
Notice trips even when the app is closed?

Eh-ligible collects your approximate location in the background, even when the app is closed or not in use, to log which country you’re in each day for your citizenship count. The check happens on your phone a few times a day; your location is never stored or sent anywhere. On the next screen, choose “Allow all the time”.
Turn on approximate location first to use background checks. You can do it later in Settings.
Background checks are on. Thank you!
Checks also run in the background
Only when the app is open
Get a nudge at milestones, on the day you can apply, and when a trip needs checking. A few a month at most.
Tip: add the Eh-ligible widget to your home screen to see your countdown every day.
Add the widget to your home screen
You have enough days to apply for citizenship. IRCC encourages applying with a few extra days, just in case.
No date in the next 15 years. Check your trips.
No trips yet. Add past or planned trips with the button below.
The day you leave and the day you come back both count as days in Canada. Only full days away are subtracted.
Same-day trip: counts as a day in Canada
This trip is in the future. It shows how your dates would move.
The return date can’t be before the departure date.
Eh-ligible couldn’t tell where you were on these days. Until you answer, they count as days outside Canada.
No removal order and no unmet conditions. An expired PR card is fine.
For at least 3 of these years, if you had to file: %1$s.
Speaking and listening in English or French, if you’re 18 to 54 on the day you sign.
Also for ages 18 to 54: 20 questions, pass mark 15.
$653 for adults (2026). IRCC updates fees every March 31.
For example: no current charges, sentence or recent conviction for a serious offence, and no recent misrepresentation.
Extra days added to get your safer date. IRCC encourages applying with more than 1,095 days.
Milestones, eligibility day and trip checks
Off: only the mobile network is used
Replace everything in the app with this backup?
That file isn’t an Eh-ligible backup.
Border data: made with Natural Earth (public domain).
Under 18, a Crown servant or Canadian Armed Forces member abroad, or had probation, parole or a sentence in the last 5 years? Eh-ligible doesn’t cover these cases. Please use IRCC’s calculator.
A quarter of the way there!
You can apply for citizenship today!
Your countdown is paused while you’re away. Have a great trip!
A few days need your review
Tap to tell Eh-ligible where you were.

string-array.name: fun_facts
string-array.item: Canada has the longest coastline of any country: about 243,000 km.
Canada is the second-largest country in the world by area.
The Canada–US border is the longest international border in the world, at about 8,890 km.
The maple leaf flag was first raised on February 15, 1965.
“O Canada” became the official national anthem in 1980.
Canada has 10 provinces and 3 territories. The newest, Nunavut, was created in 1999.
Canada holds about 20% of the world’s fresh water.
The beaver has been an official symbol of Canada since 1975.
Canada’s motto, “A mari usque ad mare”, means “From sea to sea”.
Canada borders three oceans: the Atlantic, the Pacific and the Arctic.
Basketball was invented in 1891 by a Canadian, James Naismith.
Insulin was discovered in Toronto in 1921 by Frederick Banting and Charles Best.
Canada’s highest mountain is Mount Logan in Yukon, at 5,959 m.
Lacrosse is Canada’s national summer sport and hockey its national winter sport.
Wood Buffalo National Park is bigger than Switzerland.
Canada has more lakes than any other country.
Churchill, Manitoba is known as the Polar Bear Capital of the World.
The Bay of Fundy has the highest tides in the world, up to about 16 m.
Toronto’s CN Tower was the world’s tallest free-standing structure for over 30 years.
Canada Day, July 1, marks Confederation in 1867.
Poutine, fries with cheese curds and gravy, comes from rural Quebec.
Quebec produces about 70% of the world’s maple syrup.
In winter, the Rideau Canal in Ottawa becomes a 7.8 km skating rink.
Canada’s population passed 40 million in 2023.
Canada has six time zones, including Newfoundland’s half-hour one.
The $1 coin, the loonie, arrived in 1987. The $2 toonie followed in 1996.
Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as Canada’s capital in 1857.
Banff, created in 1885, is Canada’s first national park.
The schooner Bluenose sails on the back of the Canadian dime.
Canada’s coldest recorded temperature was −63 °C, in Snag, Yukon, in 1947.
Most of Niagara’s Horseshoe Falls is on the Canadian side.
English and French are both official languages of Canada.
